- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values by 1–2% relative to model output.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < 0.2) — add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for downward bias.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — if last 3–5 days show sharp upward movement, cap forecast rise to 1–1.5x recent high.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% to align with historical volatility.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days prior, forecast should adjust downward 0.5–1.0% to reflect delayed market reaction.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation — if sentiment is volatile, use 20–30% smoothing on forecast slope to reduce overshoot.
